title: Grafana returning wrong query result after upgrading to 9.5
body: I have a Grafana stat panel backed by InfluxDB 1.8. Its query selects the last percent_packet_loss value per switch name, filters values greater than zero, and then uses a Reduce row / Count transformation. On Grafana 9.3 the panel works and currently returns 13. After upgrading to Grafana 9.5.2, the displayed result oscillates between values such as 1, 3, 6, and 8 whenever the dashboard refreshes. Downgrading to 9.3 fixes it. I am running Grafana from a package manager on Ubuntu 22.04 and viewing it in Firefox.

symptoms_visible: My stat panel returns a stable value of 13 on Grafana 9.3, but after upgrading to Grafana 9.5.2 it oscillates between values such as 1, 3, 6, and 8 whenever the dashboard refreshes.
Downgrading to Grafana 9.3 makes the panel display the expected value again.
N0.label: N0 oscillating stat value reported

symptoms_visible: The stat value still changes between refreshes on Grafana 9.5 while the Grafana 9.3 panel remains stable.
N1.label: N1 debug snapshots collected

symptoms_visible: With the transformation removed, the panels on the two Grafana versions appear to show identical results; the wrong total appears when the transformation is enabled.
N2.label: N2 behavior localized to transformation

symptoms_visible: On Grafana 9.5.6 the transformed result is still wrong even though the same InfluxDB instance is used.
N2_x.label: N2_x patch-release upgrade aftermath

symptoms_visible: With two switches down, the transformed Grafana 9.3 data contains Count 2 on both rows, while the transformed Grafana 9.5 data contains Count 1 on both rows.
N3.label: N3 transformed dataframe difference captured

symptoms_visible: With automatic field selection, the total number of switches changes incorrectly during refreshes; after I manually select all 194 device fields in the transformation, the misreadings stop.
N4.label: N4 automatic field selection isolated

symptoms_visible: After changing the InfluxDB query to count matching packet-loss records directly and continuing to add the grouped results with the transformation, the panel shows a working total and I can keep Grafana up to date.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved with query workaround

question_patterns: Can you export the panel debug data from both Grafana versions using Panel > More > Get help?
Please share panel debug snapshots for both the working and affected versions so their data can be compared.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here are both debug files: 9.5-debug-Total Switches DOWN and 9.3-debug-Total Switches DOWN.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The two debug exports already contain different query results before any transformations are applied.
I exported the same two panel snapshots again after another refresh.

edges.comment: From c0-c2: participant1 requested panel debug exports for both versions, and the reporter shared the two files from the reporter's own Grafana installations.

question_patterns: Can you remove the panel transformation and compare what both versions display?
Please disable the transformation temporarily and tell me whether the results still differ.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It indeed seems to be an issue with the transformation. With the transformation removed, the results on the two versions seem to be identical.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The values still differ between the versions with every transformation removed.
The untransformed results look the same except for their displayed timestamp formatting.

edges.comment: From c9-c11: participant4 asked the reporter to remove the transformation and compare versions; the reporter's own panels then appeared identical without it.

solution.intent: Upgrade from the affected initial 9.5 installation to a newer 9.5 patch release in case the behavior has already been corrected.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade the Grafana 9.5 installation to 9.5.6 and test the same InfluxDB-backed panel again.

edges.comment: From c19-c20: participant5 recommended upgrading to 9.5.6, but the reporter clarified that the latest tests were already on 9.5.6 and still produced the wrong transformed value.

question_patterns: Can you export the data before and after transformation from both versions?
Please download CSV data with and without transformations for the working and affected versions.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I exported all four CSV files. At the moment two switches are down. In the transformed 9.3 data, both rows have Count 2. In the transformed 9.5 data, both rows have Count 1. The InfluxDB version is exactly the same between the tests.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The transformed CSV files from both versions contain Count 2 on every row, even while the stat panel displays 1.
The same 2-versus-1 difference appears with different timestamps in a second export.

edges.comment: From c13-c20: participant5 explained how to export before/after-transformation data, and the reporter supplied obfuscated CSVs from the reporter's Grafana 9.3 and 9.5 environments.

question_patterns: Does explicitly selecting the fields used by the transformation change the result?
Please select the relevant fields manually in the transformation and report whether the incorrect readings continue.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I manually selected all 194 devices in the transformation, and the misreadings stopped. Automatic selection still gives changing totals. Selecting fields manually is not really an option for me because the fields differ with the query result and there can be dozens or hundreds of them.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same incorrect changing total remains even after I manually select every device field.
Selecting 193 of the 194 device fields gives a stable total that is one lower than expected, while selecting all 194 gives the correct total.

edges.comment: From c19-c26: participant5 proposed manually selecting fields to test a field-matching conflict; the reporter tested all 194 fields on the reporter's affected installation and observed that this stopped the misreadings.

solution.intent: Avoid the unstable automatic field-selection behavior by rewriting the InfluxDB query to count matching packet-loss records directly for each switch, then use the transformation only to add the grouped count results.
solution.concrete_example: Use `SELECT COUNT("percent_packet_loss") FROM "ping" WHERE ("bucket" = 'switches') AND ("percent_packet_loss" > 0) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY "name"`, then retain the transformation to add the per-name results. Confirm across several refreshes that the total remains correct.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established that removing the transformation makes the versions agree and that explicitly selecting all 194 fields stops the misreadings. Maintainers connected those observations to the transformation's automatic field-matching heuristic. The exact internal version-to-version change was not conclusively identified, so the diagnosis should remain at that evidence-supported level.

edges.comment: From c21-c29, especially c26-c28: the reporter demonstrated that explicit field selection avoids the error and then independently changed the query to a direct COUNT form, reporting that it worked. participant5's final technical explanation was that unspecified transformation fields are chosen by a field-matching heuristic; no Grafana code fix was landed or verified in this thread.

satisfaction_conditions: Must localize the failure to the Reduce row transformation's automatic field selection: untransformed results appeared identical, transformed CSV output differed, and explicitly selecting all 194 fields stopped the misreadings.
Must not attribute the behavior to an InfluxDB server upgrade or to the two-minute polling interval; the same InfluxDB 1.8 instance was used, and Reduce row is a frontend row-based operation.
Must not present upgrading within the affected Grafana 9.5 line as the fix, because the reporter reproduced the wrong transformed count on the newer patch release.
The accepted workaround must rewrite the InfluxQL query to count records with percent_packet_loss greater than zero per name, while retaining the transformation only to add the grouped results.
Must acknowledge that the exact underlying Grafana regression was not conclusively fixed in the thread; the reporter considered the case resolved through the working query workaround.
Must have the reporter verify that the rewritten query produces the correct stable total across refreshes before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Grafana administrator who can edit InfluxQL, export panel debug snapshots and CSV data, compare Grafana installations, and configure Telegraf, but needs explicit instructions for less familiar diagnostic exports.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven; provides requested artifacts, corrects assumptions about the environment, raises privacy concerns about hostnames and IPs, and explains why proposed manual configuration is impractical.
